name: Tarsons Products Ltd
title: Tarsons Products Ltd - 543399 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue +21% YoY to Rs 86 cr standalone with gross margin down to 67.1% on 25-50% input cost spikes; capacity still commissioning with debt at Rs 380 cr gross and no major capex planned.

utilisation.quote: our focus is shifting from capacity creation to utilization and commercialization

summary.headline: Tarsons Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR 110.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23.6% on input-cost spikes of 25-50%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR 110.2 crore and standalone revenue reached INR 86.1 crore, the company's highest Q1 standalone revenue. Domestic sales grew 17% and exports rose about 29%, with the German subsidiary Nerbe up about 6% in constant currency. Gross margin (standalone) fell to 67.1% on polymer price spikes, and consolidated EBITDA was INR 26 crore (23.6% margin), with new-facility operating costs also weighing. Management said the remaining Panchla lines are due for full commissioning in Q2, with revenue contribution from H2 FY27, and that FY27 profit will stay moderate.

segments.name: Domestic (India standalone)
segments.commentary: Grew 17% YoY; management cites a notable uptick in inquiries and an estimated domestic market of INR 1,200-1,300 crore, with government about 15-20% of it.

segments.name: Exports (India)
segments.commentary: Grew about 29% YoY after disruption from West Asia tensions and US tariffs; international price increases were close to zero, with reliance on rupee depreciation.

segments.name: Nerbe (Germany subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 6% YoY in constant currency; management says Nerbe sales will be less consistent year to year than Tarsons' India business.

guidance_outlook: Panchla and Amta contribution expected at 20-25% of standalone revenue in FY28.
Remaining capacity expected to be fully commissioned in Q2 FY27, with revenue contribution from H2 FY27.
Standalone FY27 depreciation expected at INR 105-110 crore (peak year); CWIP of about INR 160 crore to be capitalised in subsequent quarters.
Net debt expected to fall by about INR 40 crore YoY by year end; loan repayments about INR 70 crore.
Management said FY27 profit should remain relatively moderate; margins similar to Q1 levels unless input costs move sharply.
Management views ~15% growth as achievable in FY27; 20-22% seen as doable with cell culture and new products.
Expected FY28 revenue from the new product portfolio of INR 65-70 crore.
Maintenance capex expected at no more than INR 20-25 crore per year; no major new capex planned in FY27.
capex_capacity: Panchla: remaining lines still being commissioned; delay attributed to scale of projects and supplier engineering issues, now expected in H2 FY27 versus earlier guidance of start of FY27.
Capital advances about INR 20 crore and CWIP about INR 160 crore; expected to complete within Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Management estimates ~0.8x asset turnover, implying about INR 750-800 crore of peak incremental revenue from the 4-year capex plan.
Standalone FY26 depreciation INR 24.5 crore, including INR 14 crore from Panchla and INR 4 crore from Amta.
Benchtop lab equipment to be ramped up later; described as low-capex relative to plastics.
demand_pricing: Input costs for key raw materials rose 25-50%; management estimates a direct ~500 bps hit to material margin.
Partial domestic price increases taken in Q1, with full benefit expected with a one-quarter lag; international price increases close to zero.
Raw material prices peaked about six weeks before the call, fell sharply, then rose again over the last two weeks; management called the situation volatile.
Chinese competition is intense internationally (Europe, US) but limited in India, per management.
Management says recent growth came mainly from existing products, with negligible contribution from new capacity and new product categories.
Management says domestic market growth is nearing late single digits, close to pre-COVID levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Panchla commercial commissioning been delayed to H2 FY27 from the earlier start-FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the sheer number of machines and lines, supplier and engineering issues; a few months' delay on remaining lines. Q1 Panchla revenue came from existing products or capacity shifted there, with bioprocess containers and roller bottles contributing.

qa_highlights.question: What are gross and net debt, and will interest and depreciation peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR 380 crore, net debt about INR 330-340 crore. FY27 depreciation INR 105-110 crore is the peak. Interest run rate ~INR 20 crore per year, to fall in FY28. Debt reduction about INR 40 crore YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is left and what peak revenue can it support?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 160 crore CWIP and INR 20 crore capital advances to complete within Q2-Q3 FY27, no new major capex. Peak incremental revenue estimated at INR 750-800 crore on ~0.8x asset turnover.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken and what is the outlook for gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes are marginal and mostly domestic; international pricing close to zero. Management could not call the margin bottom given volatile raw material costs and said erosion is external rather than operational.

qa_highlights.question: What will it take to grow beyond 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees 20-22% as doable with new products, cell culture and export support; 15% is the base case including white labelling and contract manufacturing for export.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 expectation for Panchla and Amta and for new product revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Panchla and Amta are expected to contribute 20-25% of standalone revenue in FY28; new product portfolio revenue INR 65-70 crore in FY28. Maintenance capex no more than INR 20-25 crore a year.

risks_watch: Raw material (polymer) volatility, with a rebound in input costs over the last two weeks cited before the call.
Limited ability to pass through costs in international markets (pricing close to zero) and competitive pressure from Chinese players abroad.
Panchla line commissioning slipping further; full commissioning and H2 revenue contribution are unproven.
Export revenue lumpiness from buyer-nominated shipments, vessel availability and West Asia disruption; US tariff uncertainty.
Nerbe revenue expected to be less consistent year to year; limited integration benefits so far.
Margins expected to stay moderate in FY27, with depreciation at peak and cell culture still early-stage.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery and the capex endgame, but cautious on margins and pricing, which management repeatedly called volatile and externally driven. Management was evasive on specific price-hike percentages and on the margin floor.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 71.3 crore in Q1 FY26 (~21% YoY)
Lower, due to higher raw material (polymer) costs
Expected to continue in FY27, lower in FY28

key_quotes: Our key input costs have gone up anywhere in the range of 25% to 50%, putting pressure on gross margins.
We expect these facilities to be fully commissioned during Q2, with revenue contribution beginning from second half.
So, on a fixed asset basis, we should be able to turn in at around 0.8times.
Our standalone revenue also grew by 21% Y-o-Y and came to Rs. 86 crores, marking our highest ever Q1 standalone revenue.
It is nothing related to our internal operation metrics within the company.
We would ideally expect Panchla and Amta to at least contribute to 20% to 25% of our standalone revenues in FY'28.

adds.what: Panchla remaining production lines (Tarsons plastics capacity)

growth.why: Management views ~15% FY27 growth as achievable (20-22% with cell culture and new products), backed by Panchla/Amta lines due for commissioning in Q2 with revenue from H2 FY27 and FY28 expected new-product revenue of INR 65-70 crore, though the brief notes recent growth came mainly from existing products and Panchla has already slipped.
